headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:2.6}} on the summit of Jay Peak early Monday to Monday afternoon, and {{s:6.6}} for the week. 13 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Western Maine. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Periods of showers will continue through early next week, becoming most widespread later Saturday through Sunday morning. There is an increasing chance of light snow accumulations at higher elevations early Sunday and again Monday as colder air moves into the region.
Unsettled weather will persist through much of next week, with a general trend toward cooler weather.

ALY.excerpt:
) Scattered rain continue through tonight for locations south and east of Albany, with no flooding concerns expected.
) More widespread showers expected Saturday and Saturday night. Drier and cooler conditions are then expected for the first half of next week.

GYX.excerpt:
Two rounds of rain are expected to bring beneficial rainfall Friday through Saturday night with heaviest amounts expected for the immediate coast with lighter amounts for mountains.
Cooler temperatures arrive later this weekend through the middle of next week areawide. There will be multiple chances for light precipitation, including light snow or snow showers for the higher peaks of the White Mountains.

BUF.excerpt: ) Unsettled weather and cooler temperatures today through the weekend.

PHI.excerpt: A slow moving cold front will cross the area through today bringing several rounds of rain, heavy at times.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild through today with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell now over.
) Trending cooler this weekend with lake enhanced rain showers beneath upper level low, mixing with some wet snow showers early Sat across the NW Mtns and Laurel Highlands .

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Some snow early Monday, best at Jay Peak.
paras: Light snow early Monday to Monday afternoon: Jay Peak {{s:2.6}}, Smugglers' Notch {{s:2.2}}, Stowe {{s:2.2}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.3,7}} at Jay Peak. It's a northwest upslope setup, one that usually favors Jay Peak, Smugglers' Notch and Stowe. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:29}} to {{t:56}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 22).

NWS Burlington forecasters, Friday 6:30 AM: "Periods of showers will continue through early next week, becoming most widespread later Saturday through Sunday morning. There is an increasing chance of light snow accumulations at higher elevations early Sunday and again Monday as colder air moves into the region."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

paras: Light snow Saturday night to Sunday morning: Bretton Woods {{s:1.2}}, Cannon {{s:1.1}}, Wildcat {{s:0.9}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.5,5.8}} at Bretton Woods. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:38}} to {{t:59}}, with rain at times.
Bretton Woods usually opens first here, around Nov 15. Cannon gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 19).

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:2.6}} at the summit early Monday to Monday afternoon (models {{r:0.3,7}}). Snow level near {{e:2000}}, so the base ({{e:1800}}) mixes with or changes to rain early Monday: about {{s:0}} there vs {{s:2.6}} up top. Highs stay near {{t:34}} afterward, so some of it should stick up high.
Cold enough to make snow early Thursday to Thursday night: about 22 hours at or below {{t:26}} at mid-mountain, counting humidity. Whether the guns run is up to the resort.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 21 days out.
